abstract: Audits airborne particulate levels and upper bay thermal calibration data
system_message:
You are Cleanroom metrology lead (CLM). The Cleanroom metrology lead (CLM) audits airborne particulate levels and upper bay thermal calibration data across evaluated reticle storage vault designs. In addition, this lead oversees optical inspection metrology for silicon test specimens within the cleanroom storage environment.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Audits airborne particulate levels and upper bay thermal calibration data（PART）
information_points.content:
CLM-PART-RFV：For the Modular Inert-Gas Isolator Enclosure, airborne particulate ISO Class 1 compliance is true within the active internal storage volume, while the upper vault bay thermal drift is recorded at 24 mK across the upper reticle carousel racks during the 48-hour thermal hold.
CLM-PART-CMC：For the Suspended Active-Damping Micro-Chamber, airborne particulate ISO Class 1 compliance is false across the active internal volume, and the upper vault bay thermal drift measures 12 mK during the 48-hour hold.
CLM-PART-POY：For the Subterranean Deep-Bed Pneumatic Vault, airborne particulate ISO Class 1 compliance is true based on cleanroom airborne particle count surveys of the active internal storage volume, and the upper vault bay thermal drift is 12 mK as measured across upper reticle carousel racks over a 48-hour thermal hold.

information_points.title: Optical inspection metrology（OPT）
information_points.content:
CLM-OPT-DUO：Optical inspection metrology records show that the Modular Inert-Gas Isolator Enclosure exhibits an interferometric surface roughness deviation of 0.18 nm on reference silicon wafer test specimens.
CLM-OPT-QD2：Optical inspection metrology logs indicate that the Subterranean Deep-Bed Pneumatic Vault exhibits an interferometric surface roughness deviation of 0.12 nm on reference silicon wafer test specimens.
CLM-OPT-XWN：According to optical inspection metrology reports, the Suspended Active-Damping Micro-Chamber demonstrates an interferometric surface roughness deviation of 0.24 nm on reference silicon wafer test specimens.
